演奏時將竹管一端置於唇邊，向藤圈與竹管間的小孔縫隙吹氣；手指覆蓋音孔，以指法改變: To play, the player sets one end of the bamboo tube at the lips and blows into the gap between the rattan ring and the small hole in the tube; the fingers cover the fingerholes, changing the resonating wavelength, and the speed of the airstream and the position of the embouchure set the pitch. A beginner first steadies the breath and practises single notes and slides; Balinese pieces need circular breathing to keep the tone continuous. The Maguindanao type is blown through a hole at the bottom, with five holes above and one at the bottom controlling the pitch.

蘇林笛具有溫潤而柔和的音色，散發著東南亞竹樂器特有的溫暖韻味。其音色既不過於明亮: The suling has a warm, soft timbre, giving off the warmth that is particular to Southeast Asian bamboo instruments. Its tone is neither too bright and harsh nor dull and dark, but quiet and reserved. Its range lies mainly in the upper middle register, and it carries well, sounding clearly even over the thick accompaniment of a degung ensemble. Its resonance depends on the natural resonance of the bamboo tube, which gives the timbre a bamboo warmth. Against the bright clarity of the dizi, the suling sounds steadier; against the heaviness of the ocarina, it is more nimble. This particular sound makes it an indispensable melodic instrument of traditional Sundanese music.
蘇林笛為氣鳴樂器，琴身主要用竹管製作，來源指明多為塔米昂竹，其管長而壁薄。吹口端: The suling is an aerophone, its body made mainly from a bamboo tube, which the source identifies mostly as tamiang bamboo, long and thin-walled. At the blowing end a fine rattan strip is wound into a ring close to a small hole, and the player sounds the instrument by blowing into the gap between the ring and the tube. The source gives no separate materials for the fingerholes, the blowing hole and the other openings, or for the extra parts of regional forms.
蘇林笛為氣鳴樂器，見於東南亞。印尼巽他音樂中，它是德貢合奏成員，也用於卡查皮蘇林: The suling is an aerophone found in Southeast Asia. In Indonesian Sundanese music it is a member of the degung ensemble, is also used in kacapi suling, and accompanies gamelan degung and Sundanese song. In Balinese music the suling is an important instrument, and players use circular breathing to keep a continuous tone alongside the gamelan percussion. At cultural festivals and other events in Brunei it plays with traditional instruments such as the gulintangan. In Sabah, Malaysia, it is played by inland peoples such as the Kadazan-Dusun, Murut, Rungus and Lun Bawang / Lundayeh; in Sarawak it is played mostly by men in the Dayak longhouse. The suling of the Maguindanao in the Philippines is the smallest bamboo flute, and because the palendag is hard to play, it and the tumpong have become the common aerophones.
蘇林笛（Suling）是印尼巽他人的氣鳴樂器，作為竹環笛在東南亞多地流傳。它在巽: The suling is an aerophone of the Sundanese of Indonesia, a bamboo ring flute found in many parts of Southeast Asia. In Sundanese music it is used in the degung ensemble, in kacapi suling and to accompany Sundanese song; in Balinese music it keeps a continuous tone with circular breathing. Its development can be read in the number of holes: four holes serve a single mode, six can play at least three modes, and seven to nine serve extended modes such as mandalungan. In the Maguindanao region of the Philippines, because the palendag is harder to play, the suling and the tumpong have replaced it as the common aerophones.
蘇林笛（Suling）是東南亞竹製環笛，H-S編號421.211.12，屬氣鳴樂: The suling is a bamboo ring flute of Southeast Asia, H-S number 421.211.12, an aerophone. It is common in Indonesia, Brunei, Malaysia, the Philippines and Singapore; the Sundanese of Indonesia use it in the degung ensemble, in kacapi suling and to accompany Sundanese song. It is mostly made of tamiang bamboo with thin walls; at the blowing end a rattan ring circles a small hole, the player blows into the gap between the ring and the tube, changes the resonating wavelength with the fingerholes, and sets the pitch by the speed of the air.
